request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

agent.result_text:
All the sheets of a tree now share one claim-number sequence, and all 4 tests pass when run with `bin/e2e`.

**What changed** — only `ClaimRepository.nextNumber` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/ClaimRepository.java`:
- When a claim is opened, it looks up the sheet's whole tree (the sheet plus every sheet above and below it) using the existing `SheetRepository.tree()`.
- It gives out one more than the highest last number on any sheet in the tree. It then records that number as the last one on every sheet in the tree, all in one database statement, so two claims opened at once can't get the same number.
- Numbers already given stay as they are. For example, a parent and a child that each already had claim 1 continue together at 2, 3, and so on.
- Numbering by period (like `P1-1`) still runs separately on each sheet; that code wasn't touched.
- Every other place that numbers claims goes through this same method, so they all follow the shared sequence too: opening a claim, opening several at once, splitting, moving a claim to another person, moving a person to another sheet, and cloning a sheet.

**Two things to know:**
- `ClaimRepository` now takes `SheetRepository` as a second constructor argument.
- The test doesn't check two claims being opened at the same moment across sheets of one tree. Duplicate numbers in that case depend on how the H2 database locks rows during the update; I haven't tested it.

No changes were needed to the stored data, the endpoints or the front end.
